topics.topic: Operation and failure semantics for reading manifest bytes at a configured revision
questions: What operation resolves a manifest location plus revision into the exact service-record bytes, and what failures does it return?
How must `bindings` obtain that file at the named revision, and what failures mean that the revision or file cannot be read?

quotes: manifest_source: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns ManifestSource with manifest_location and manifest_revision of the Installation loaded at start, unchanged until restart.

read_service_record: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] A service_id that does not match the imported SERVICE_ID_PATTERN constant raises RefusedError before any path is built; the record is read only as the git object of the file named service_id followed by the imported MANIFEST_RECORD_FILE_SUFFIX constant inside manifest_location at manifest_revision, both from manifest_source, and no other path, revision or name is searched.

read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.
judgement.why: The later notes define read_service_record as reading the named Git object at the configured revision and specify its ordered failures.

topics.topic: Representation of successful outputs in try_implementation responses
questions: Does the direct `try_implementation` response contain successful JSON output values, StoredValue references, or only output digests?
Does an explicit try return only output digests, complete TrialExecution records with non-personal JSON outputs resolved, or StoredValue references?

quotes: handle_try_implementation: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST call try_implementation with the implementation_id, the trial_case_ids in request order and the actor, and show each returned TrialExecution under the surface masking rule, its outputs through show_port_refs and its failure_detail masked by the class of that execution.

show_port_refs: [FIELD_PROJECTION] For each PortRef, in order, MUST produce one ShownPort with the same port name and one ShownItem per referenced item in order: a StoredValuesRef reads its StoredValue records with read_records using RecordsById, and a value carriage item becomes ShownContent with its value_id, its canonical JSON text read with read_value_bytes from a StoredValueSource and its class, a file carriage item becomes ShownFile with digest, size, media type, class, its value_id and no spooled_file; a SpooledFilesRef reads its SpooledFile records with SpooledFilesByKey and each becomes ShownFile carrying its full SpooledFileKey and no value_id; a FileFactsRef becomes one ShownFile per FileFacts with the class the FileFactsRef carries, no spooled_file and no value_id.

show_port_refs: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] This is the one masking rule of every answer: the owner receives every item in full; when reader is not of kind owner and an item's class is personal_data, MUST produce ShownValueDigest with the value digest and class for a value, or ShownFileDigest with the content digest and class for a file, and read no bytes for it (A07 rule 4).
handle_try_implementation: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns one ShownTrialExecution per execution, in the order try_implementation returned them.
judgement.why: The later notes require complete shown trial-execution records, resolving non-personal value outputs to canonical JSON content and masking personal-data outputs to digest and class.

topics.topic: Scope and ordering of A08 startup manifest validation
questions: Which A08 checks are performed at start, on which capability entries, and in what order when several entries fail?

With no operation or proposal ports supplied at startup, which A08 checks are checks of the service record itself, and must startup validate every capability or only the top-level record and selected instance facts needed for header collision checking?

quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
judgement.why: The later notes limit startup validation to credential-bearing services, ordered by service_id, and to top-level service-record checks plus the selected instance's credential-header collision.

topics.topic: Whether runs may call bindings.read_binding for operation-port facts
questions: May `runs` call `bindings.read_binding`, or must operation-port facts reach `runs` through another operation or caller?
May `runs` call `bindings.read_binding` to obtain operation-port definitions needed for readiness and input validation?

quotes:
### Knows

`models`, `data_provider`, `canonical_values`, `clock`, `store`, `sandbox`,
`functions` (current activation, a function node's ports), `bindings` (an
operation node's ports, through `bindings.read_binding`), `flows` (active
version), `effects`.
judgement.why: State 3 explicitly makes runs a consumer of bindings.read_binding, while State 5's exhaustive caller list excludes runs.

topics.topic: Allowed base URL forms and exact path-joining rules
questions: Are base URLs with multiple trailing slashes, a path prefix, query, fragment, user information or unusual authority spelling allowed, and exactly how are they joined to the declared path?

topics.topic: Atomic rollback and cleanup-failure result when spool_file refuses a ceiling breach
questions: Is removal of all earlier files from the attempt atomic with the refusal, and what result is returned if that cleanup cannot be completed?

topics.topic: Capability returned by monotonic_deadline and ownership of later monotonic reads
questions: What exact capability does the caller receive for checking and waiting on the deadline, and which component performs the monotonic reads after creation?

topics.topic: Continuation-token semantics when records do not match page filters
questions: Does "more remain" mean more records of the type below the cursor or more records that currently match the filter, and can an empty or short page carry a continuation token over currently nonmatching records?

topics.topic: Definition of a loopback host for the plain-HTTP exception
questions: What exactly counts as a loopback host: only canonical IP literals, every IP literal classified as loopback, the name `localhost`, or a hostname whose DNS result is loopback?

topics.topic: Error returned for missing references in add_captured_trial_case
questions: What error is returned when the implementation, source execution input reference or SpooledFile named by the internal capture call does not exist?

topics.topic: Fixed data used to classify and mask TrialExecution disclosures
questions: From what fixed data does `surface` derive the class used to mask a TrialExecution's `failure_detail` and file-output facts?

topics.topic: Handling of response Content-Encoding and timing of response-size enforcement
questions: Does the invoker reject a non-identity content encoding, decode it, or treat the encoded entity bytes as the response body, and at which stage is the response-size ceiling applied?

topics.topic: Handling successful trial outputs that exceed stored_value_bytes_max
questions: What happens when a trial or admission execution succeeds within `output_bytes` but a value output exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`?

topics.topic: How content_identity identifies content-record kinds requiring sorted lists
questions: How does the operation distinguish an ordinary JSON value containing similarly named lists from a particular content-record kind whose lists must be sorted?

topics.topic: How later operations select the loaded installation and configuration
questions: How do later installation operations know which loaded installation and configuration file to use?

topics.topic: How later operations select the opened store and who owns its handle and lock
questions: How is the opened store selected by later store operations, and who owns the returned handle and lock lifetime?

topics.topic: Multipart boundary selection and collision prevention
questions: How is the multipart boundary chosen, and how must the kernel ensure that it cannot collide with any value or file part content?

topics.topic: Referential validation and malformed-payload handling in store.record_change
questions: For each named change, exactly which referenced identities and links must `store` verify, and which malformed payloads are `internal_error` rather than accepted on caller trust?

topics.topic: Representation enabling canonical_bytes to detect duplicate JSON keys
questions: What representation reaches `canonical_bytes` when duplicate-member detection is required?

topics.topic: Treatment of duplicate port declarations during request-shape checking
questions: How does request-shape checking treat duplicate input or output port names, especially when the duplicate declarations have different carriage or schemas?

topics.topic: Which retry attempt determines the current operation element conclusion
questions: Which attempt determines the current element conclusion when several attempts exist, and how are older unresolved or resolved records treated?

topics.topic: failure_detail policy for transport failures without a response body
questions: For transport failures without a response body, is `failure_detail` absent, a fixed kernel phrase, or sanitized transport-library text?
